The air in the auditorium hummed, not with anticipation, but with the nervous thrum of machinery. June navigated the maze of cables and scaffolding, her sensible shoes clicking softly on the polished concrete floor. Dr. Alistair Finch, a man whose brilliance was only surpassed by his disorganization, was wrestling with a tangle of fiber optic lines. Strands escaped his grasp, resembling a metallic Medusa attempting to ensnare him.

“Need a hand, Doctor?” June asked, her voice calm amidst the controlled chaos. She was a specialist in logistical support for scientific demonstrations – essentially, the person who ensured genius didn’t accidentally electrocute itself. Finch barely registered her presence, muttering about impedance and refractive indices. He was, as usual, entirely absorbed in the intricate dance of his creation. 

The creation itself dominated the stage. It resembled a geodesic dome constructed from shimmering, opalescent panels. Inside, a complex network of lasers pulsed with a slow, rhythmic beat, painting the interior with shifting patterns of light. Finch called it the "Chrono-Resonator," a device purported to manipulate temporal fields, allowing for the observation – and, eventually, interaction – with echoes of the past. The publicity surrounding it had been immense. 

June bypassed the Doctor and began systematically organizing the auxiliary equipment. A bank of monitors displayed fluctuating graphs and arcane calculations. A console bristled with switches and dials, labeled with terms she barely understood. She checked the power levels, confirmed the cooling systems were functioning optimally, and ensured the emergency shut-off was clearly marked. These were the practicalities, the grounding forces that tethered Finch’s fantastical ambitions to reality.

A small knot of reporters had already gathered near the back of the auditorium, their cameras poised like predatory birds. A few eager students perched on the balcony, notebooks open, ready to transcribe every word of Finch’s presentation. The auditorium staff, a collection of weary-looking technicians and security personnel, moved with practiced efficiency, preparing for the influx of attendees.

Finch finally managed to subdue the fiber optic rebellion, letting out a small, triumphant grunt. He straightened his tie, a vibrant paisley that clashed spectacularly with his tweed jacket. “June, dear girl,” he said, turning to her with a distracted smile, “Are we ready to make history?” He adjusted the microphone, the gesture radiating an unsettling combination of pride and anxiety. 

June offered a professional smile in return. "Everything is in order, Doctor. The audience will be here shortly.” She double-checked the final readings on her tablet, the numbers displaying a reassuring green.  The demonstration was set to begin.
